message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"7.7","text":"Knowing, then, both these good and evil actions, I announce them to you beforehand as two roads, showing you along which one people perish as they walk and along which one they are saved as they travel, guided by God. The road of those who perish is broad and very smooth, but it brings destruction without toil; the road of those who are saved is narrow and rough, but at the end it saves those who have traversed it laboriously. At the head of these two roads sit unbelief and faith. Those who have preferred pleasures travel by way of unbelief; because of those pleasures . . . . they did not even continue to seek what is beneficial. Yet they do not know that God’s purposes are not like human purposes. For first of all, he knows everyone’s thoughts, and each person is held accountable not only for undertaking something but also for intending it. Those who try to think what is good and fail act far less impiously than those who do not attempt good things at all. For God himself saw fit that the person who lapses despite knowing what is good should, after being punished moderately in proportion to human transgressions, be saved. But those who have neglected even to begin to know what is better—even if they do countless other good things—but do not adopt the religious observance he himself prescribed will, having incurred a charge of negligence, be utterly extinguished by the greatest punishment.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"προκαθέζεται ἀπιστία καὶ πίστις","chosen":"At the head of these two roads sit unbelief and faith","rationale":"προκάθημαι depicts unbelief and faith as positioned before or at the head of their respective roads."},{"source_quote":"δι’ ἃς . . . . οὐδὲ ζητεῖν τὸ συμφέρον οὐ διεφύλαξαν","chosen":"because of those pleasures . . . . they did not even continue to seek what is beneficial","rationale":"δι’ ἃς refers back to the pleasures, while διαφυλάσσω with the infinitive is understood as maintaining or continuing an activity. The two negatives are treated as emphatic negative concord; a strictly logical double-negative reading is possible in isolation but is contextually less likely. The exact four-dot gap is preserved because its unavailable wording prevents recovery of the complete causal statement."},{"source_quote":"οὐκ ἐν τῷ ἐνχειρῆσαι μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῷ ἐννοῆσαι","chosen":"not only for undertaking something but also for intending it","rationale":"The contrast extends accountability from beginning an action to conceiving or intending it; “something” and “it” represent the implicit object shared by the two infinitives. “Conceiving it” is also possible for ἐννοῆσαι."},{"source_quote":"οἱ ἐγχειροῦντες καλὰ νοεῖν καὶ ἀποτυγχάνοντες","chosen":"Those who try to think what is good and fail","rationale":"The rendering preserves νοεῖν as mental activity rather than adding an action not explicitly stated; “try to understand good things” is a viable lexical alternative."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ λόγον τῶν ἀνθρωπίνων παραπτωμάτων μετρίως κολασθέντα","chosen":"after being punished moderately in proportion to human transgressions","rationale":"κατὰ λόγον is attached to the punishment and expresses proportion. It could instead qualify the person’s lapse as occurring according to the measure or character of human transgressions, but its placement before μετρίως κολασθέντα permits the chosen attachment."},{"source_quote":"ἐν ᾗ δὲ αὐτὸς ὥρισεν θρησκείᾳ μὴ γένωνται","chosen":"but do not adopt the religious observance he himself prescribed","rationale":"Literally, they do not “come to be in” the θρησκεία he determined. “Religious observance” preserves the practical cultic or devotional sense; “religion” or “worship” is also possible in this context."},{"source_quote":"ἀποσβεσθήσονται","chosen":"will be utterly extinguished","rationale":"The verb retains the image of quenching or extinguishing rather than being generalized to “will be punished” or “will perish”; “utterly” represents παντελῶς."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"δι’ ἃς . . . . οὐδὲ ζητεῖν τὸ συμφέρον οὐ διεφύλαξαν","issue":"The selected edition prints exactly four dots between the surviving opening causal phrase and the surviving negative clause. The unavailable wording leaves the complete causal statement fragmentary, and no restoration has been supplied. The image-checked transcription verifies the printed gap but does not recover its content. Under the selected-edition coverage scope, the translation preserves the exact gap marker and defensibly represents all surviving words, so the unavailable content does not itself block publication.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἄνευ του πόνου","issue":"The article is printed as του without the expected circumflex. This is an accentual feature and does not affect the meaning.","proposed_reading":"ἄνευ τοῦ πόνου","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἐνχειρῆσαι","issue":"The print has the orthographic form ἐνχειρῆσαι where the assimilated compound spelling ἐγχειρῆσαι is more usual. The supplied form remains intelligible as the aorist infinitive of “undertake.”","proposed_reading":"ἐγχειρῆσαι","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
